description: Show this command catalog. Add a word to filter, like groundwork-help git or groundwork-help update.
Fuzzy-pick a command from the catalog with fzf; prints it and copies it to the clipboard when possible.

Open the complete local Groundwork site from the checkout chezmoi is actually using. Resolves visible ~/code and legacy ~/.local/share/chezmoi source layouts instead of trusting a copied file:// path; prints the exact path on headless platforms.

The one normal maintenance command: under one machine-wide lock, pull and apply Groundwork, resume in the freshly applied runner, upgrade the exact Homebrew packages declared in the checksum-safe Brewfile plus other managed tools, then run supported package-manager maintenance and label-scoped Docker scratch cleanup. If the selected macOS Docker backend is stopped, an interactive run may offer to start it only for the tidy and restore the stopped state; the default is no and noninteractive runs never start it. The final receipt separates current/no-change, maintenance, owner-review, preserved warning, failed, and pending-repair outcomes. On macOS, the final health check also offers a verified Karabiner restart for an unusually large footprint or observed version change. Unmanaged Homebrew software stays untouched; Chrome uses its profile-selected vendor-updated lane. Failures preserve completed work, record pending state, exit nonzero, and keep reminding until repaired.

Exceptional fast refresh: synchronize and upgrade tools but skip package-manager and Docker scratch maintenance. It never clears existing pending maintenance and exits nonzero if an earlier maintenance failure still needs repair.

Advanced read-only report: Homebrew/npm cache sizes; exact trusted pnpm candidates with store, size, pin, representative repository, and all selectors; machine-wide cadence; conflicts, custom stores, and unmatched generations for owner review. Changes no persistent state.
Run supported Homebrew and npm maintenance now, plus exact-pinned trusted pnpm stores when the machine-wide cadence or pending repair says due.

Exceptional override: attempt normal Homebrew and npm maintenance and every eligible pnpm candidate immediately, ignoring pnpm cadence. Routine retries use update-all, or groundwork-cleanup --yes when upgrades should not repeat. Repository dependency installations such as node_modules are not modified; Homebrew may remove installed orphan formula dependencies, while requested formulae/casks remain.

Acknowledge one pending homebrew, npm, pnpm, or maintenance-helper reminder that cannot be repaired because its manager was intentionally removed. Clears only Groundwork's reminder, performs no cleanup, and preserves an audit note.

Canonical settings editor for mutable preferences, including environment role, release posture, terminal multiplexer (Herdr/tmux/both/none), and Xcode beta. Existing tmux users stay on tmux until they change it. Other settings change only when selected, with preview and confirmation; accepting applies the selected desired state immediately.
Start the configured primary multiplexer. Herdr is primary for Herdr/Both, tmux for tmux, None refuses, and an existing Herdr/tmux environment refuses automatic nesting.
Print the stable machine-readable terminalMultiplexer selection, installed set, primary/fallback roles, and disabled-nesting contract.
Read-only report of the effective Herdr config and Groundwork's exact ownership receipt.
Compare the effective Herdr config with Groundwork's exact source template.
Edit Groundwork's Herdr source template through chezmoi; apply after review.
Remove only an unchanged receipt-matching Groundwork Herdr config; preserve the binary, sessions, agent settings, and user changes.
Inspect Herdr's official agent integration state.
Explicitly install Herdr's official Claude Code and Codex hooks for agent tools detected on this machine; never runs during chezmoi apply.
Explicitly delegate removal of detected Claude Code/Codex hooks to Herdr's supported integration lifecycle.
Inspect the Herdr server and client state.
Show installed Herdr agent integration versions and state.
Detach the Herdr client while the live server and pane processes continue.
Show Herdr's active keybindings.
Enter Herdr copy mode.
Report the current platform as darwin, linux, wsl2, wsl1, wsl-unknown, or unsupported.
On Linux or WSL, report the distribution ID; --family reports its bootstrap family (debian, fedora, arch, opensuse, or unknown).
Show the bootstrap seed, saved environment role, application release posture, terminal multiplexer selection, Xcode and Xcode-beta status, headless state, and detected operating-system channel.

Focused shortcut into groundwork-configure's guarded preview-and-confirm transaction for stable versus preview release posture. Confirming applies the selected desired state immediately; update-all owns later upgrades and maintenance.
Open the chezmoi config when the role, preset, or another profile field needs direct review.

Copy the last completed command and its output into a tmux buffer (and the clipboard when supported); a platform + directory line is prepended so pasted output tells an agent where it ran. Review for secrets before pasting into an AI tool.
Copy the current pane's working directory to the clipboard (native OSC 52 via a helper that reads the path from tmux and never runs it through a shell).
Zoom the active pane to fill the screen; press again to restore. The status line shows Z while zoomed — this is what happened if a pane suddenly took over the screen.
Repo picker popup: fuzzy-search every repository discovered under your configured roots, preview its git status, and jump to (or open) its lazygit window.
Open a lazygit window for every repository with uncommitted changes (groundwork-repos changed).
Close the active pane. It asks first, because x sits next to z (zoom).
Start a selection while browsing tmux pane history.
Toggle a rectangular selection while browsing tmux pane history.
Copy the selection to the tmux buffer and supported system clipboard, then leave copy mode.
Drag with the mouse to select in a pane; the selection copies to the tmux buffer and system clipboard the moment you release. Convenient, but it replaces whatever the clipboard held.
In a mouse-aware app, forward right-click to the app; in an ordinary shell pane, show the copy-model hint.
Open tmux's pane menu without taking ordinary right-click away from mouse-aware apps.
Send a literal Ctrl+a to the program inside the active pane.
Rename the active tmux session.
Split the active pane left and right in its current directory.
Split the active pane top and bottom in its current directory.
Create a new window in the active pane's current directory.
Move to the pane on the left.
Move to the pane below.
Move to the pane above.
Move to the pane on the right.
Clear the visible shell screen and tmux's retained history for the active pane.
Resize the active pane five cells to the left.
Resize the active pane five cells downward.
Resize the active pane five cells upward.
Resize the active pane five cells to the right.
Move the active window one position to the left.
Move the active window one position to the right.

Open lazygit for the active pane's current repository.
Open the session switcher; inside it, Ctrl+x closes the highlighted live session.
Preview dotfile changes before applying them to your home directory.
Apply the source repo to your home directory.
Git pull the Groundwork repo and apply it; --init keeps every setup answer and asks only newly added questions. Syncs config, not already-installed tool upgrades.
Edit a managed dotfile at its source instead of editing the generated home file.
Open a shell in the Groundwork source repo.
Restore the first-run backup of managed files and macOS defaults.

Read-only machine health report. Its default run checks shell/runtime/tool ownership, the selected browser, Karabiner compatibility and process memory on macOS, and Docker health and leftovers. An unusually large Karabiner footprint includes the exact repair command. It never changes settings or state.

Run only the Docker section, including report-only detection of old unlabeled Groundwork validation tags that bypassed the scratch lifecycle. The documented groundwork:latest runnable tag is excluded.
Run only the shell runtime section: managed zsh installed, registered, selected as login shell, and running here.
Flag any mise-managed runtime adopted inside the 5-day release floor. A cooldown filters what you acquire; it never rolls back what you already have.

Run only the default report's Karabiner section: version and compatibility, current macOS support, root Core Service PID, owner, elapsed time, RSS, memory footprint, compressed memory, and an exact restart recommendation when the shared review threshold is met. One snapshot is not a growth rate or diagnosis.

Request Karabiner's documented user-domain restart and wait up to 10 seconds for a different root Core Service PID. No changed PID means failure and menu/Settings guidance; private root launch daemons stay untouched.

Opt-in read-only storage report (skipped by the default run because du over large trees is slow): sizes of the known large developer areas (Homebrew cache, pnpm store generations, npm cache, Xcode device support and simulators, a legacy ~/.nvm, Parallels VMs), each classified and paired with the command or app surface that owns cleaning it. Curated, not a full disk scan; reports only, never deletes.

Report who owns Node and pnpm on this machine: the active Node, Corepack or competing pnpm ownership, every distinct pnpm owner on PATH, repository pins, nested-process agreement, and any pnpm global-tool directory outside PATH. Explains project-local tools and the five-day-floor personal mise npm-tool lane without running pnpm setup.
Report whether Yazi's effective yazi.toml is absent, exactly Groundwork-owned, changed, unowned, or non-regular. Read-only.
Preview the effective Yazi yazi.toml against Groundwork's exact source template without changing either file.
Open Groundwork's exact Yazi source template through chezmoi; run chezmoi apply afterward to apply the reviewed source.
Remove only an unchanged yazi.toml that matches Groundwork's exact ownership receipt. Other Yazi files and user changes are preserved; chezmoi apply restores the managed file.

Dry-run Docker tidy, by enumeration: every image labeled dev.roost.ephemeral=true is inspected and reported as eligible (past the 72h grace by its strict-parsed dev.roost.built label, exactly one scratch-namespace tag, no container references), retained (in grace), protected (multiple tags, a non-scratch tag, or a container reference), or unverified (missing jq or missing/malformed build label — retained, never removed); exited containers carrying the label are judged by the same grace window against their CreatedAt. Never volumes, never unlabeled images, never dangling images or builder cache.

Remove the eligible set: exited containers labeled dev.roost.ephemeral=true whose CreatedAt is past the same 72h grace, then each eligible image — all re-checked immediately before explicit-ID deletion. Per-call and total-lane deadlines bound the transaction; update-all uses the fixed-budget canonical local-only --automatic mode. Daemon-wide cleanup remains separate.
Acknowledge the Docker scratch reminder only after Docker was intentionally removed and cleanup cannot be retried. Performs no Docker query or deletion and preserves a timestamped audit note.

Dry-run preview of the DAEMON-WIDE cleanup: stopped containers, dangling images, and builder cache from every project on this machine, not just Groundwork. Owner-run only — update-all and scheduled agent paths never invoke it.

Apply bounded daemon-wide cleanup through a trusted CLI against a verified local Unix endpoint: prune stopped containers and dangling images, and prune builder cache toward the 5GB retention target (--keep-storage asks Docker to retain a target; it is not a guarantee). Remote daemons, volumes, and tagged images are never touched.

Single-directory diagnostic: dry-run report of every pnpm store generation and the store selected by the current directory. The automatic machine-maintenance path is update-all; use this narrower command when diagnosing one repository's selection.

Run pnpm store prune on the store selected by the current directory, re-checked (store and version) immediately before pruning — a moved selection or a packageManager pin that disagrees with the resolved pnpm is refused — with a measured before/after/reclaimed receipt. Projects are not modified; pruned packages re-download on next use. Other store generations are never touched — another repository's packageManager may select them.

Build and remove a proof-only Docker image under the ephemeral contract: the wrapper owns both labels, the scratch tag, and the image ID. Inside Groundwork, use scripts/verify-docker-image when the proof must run the image.

Inside the Groundwork repository, use a trusted CLI against a verified local Unix endpoint to mechanically build, smoke-run, and remove a uniquely tagged scratch image by its exact image ID. CID-file ownership and bounded EXIT/HUP/INT/TERM cleanup make removal independent of whether the smoke test succeeds; a repointed tag is reported and never removed.

Make Groundwork's Homebrew zsh your login shell (records your current shell first, registers the new one in /etc/shells, runs chsh, verifies the account record). Your previous shell stays untouched as the recovery path.
Report the shell runtime state (managed zsh, account login shell, $SHELL, recorded previous shell) and change nothing.
Restore the login shell you had before adopting. Works even when Homebrew is unavailable.
Restore a specific login shell, for when no previous one was recorded.

Table of every Git repository discovered under your configured roots (~/.config/groundwork/repos.conf): branch, dirty/clean as symbol + word, ahead/behind, worktree marker, path. Discovery is dynamic — a fresh clone appears within the cache TTL (30s), or immediately with --refresh, no config edit.

Fuzzy-pick a discovered repository (fzf) with a live git-status preview, then open or reuse its lazygit tmux window. Inside tmux it becomes a window; outside, it creates or attaches the repos session.
Open one lazygit tmux window per repository with uncommitted work — the fastest way to see everything your agents left unreviewed.
Scaffold AGENTS.md, agent folders, editor settings, and .gitignore for a new repo.
Scaffold a Groundwork Twelve learning log, initialize it as a Git repo, and enter it; defaults to ~/groundwork-log.
Scaffold a private agent-maintained knowledge wiki with raw/wiki layers and Obsidian setup.
Copy selected files or folders to the clipboard with path headers and contents for AI review.
Install the Groundwork-managed Obsidian plugin set into a vault.
Sign in to GitHub for gh and HTTPS Git operations.
Configure gh as Git's HTTPS credential helper in an unmanaged Git config. Groundwork already renders the equivalent helper block, so this is normally unnecessary here.
List files with details, hidden files, Git status, and directories first.
List files with eza, grouping directories first.
Hidden-inclusive tree view, two levels deep, honoring Git ignores and excluding .git internals. Pass a path to inspect only that path.
Hidden-inclusive tree view, three levels deep, honoring Git ignores and excluding .git internals. Pass a path to inspect only that path.
Open lazygit.
Open Neovim.
Use bat for syntax-highlighted file viewing.
Jump to a frecent folder with zoxide.
Fuzzy-pick a folder, including hidden developer folders while honoring ignores and excluding .git internals; preview it as a tree and cd into it.
Fuzzy-pick files, including hidden developer files while honoring ignores and excluding .git internals; preview with bat and insert the chosen paths.
Open Yazi with developer dotfiles initially visible; period toggles them, q quits into the browsed folder, and Q returns to the starting folder.
Show the 50 largest files and folders under a path, followed by safe cleanup guidance for each result type.
Show only the largest files under a path; use / for the startup filesystem.
Show only the largest folders under a path; add -n N to change the result count.
Create a folder, including parent folders if needed.
Print the current folder path.
Open the current folder in Finder.
Search file contents quickly. Lowercase searches are case-insensitive by default.
Search hidden and gitignored files too, while still skipping .git internals.
Search hidden files while preserving ignore rules and excluding .git internals.
Search hidden and ordinary files while preserving ignore rules, fuzzy-pick a result, preview it with bat, and open it in the editor.
Find files by name quickly.
Find hidden and ordinary paths while preserving ignore rules and excluding .git internals.
Search shell history with atuin/fzf.
Run Atuin's opt-in English-to-shell assistant after setup.
List or set the macOS default browser; Groundwork never changes it automatically.
List or open the recommended Chrome extension links.
List or open the recommended Raycast Store extension links.
BetterDisplay command-line interface for display automation.
Open a macOS app from the shell.
Pin a runtime/tool version in the current project.
Upgrade globally managed mise tools, including floating baselines such as Node LTS. Takes effect at your next prompt, even in already-open terminals.
Package manager installed through mise for JavaScript projects.
Python installed and versioned by mise; avoid relying on macOS system Python.
Fast Python package, project, script, tool, and virtualenv manager.
Show changed files.
Show unstaged changes.
Interactively stage parts of a change.
Commit staged changes.
Show the latest commit summary.

List local branches, newest commit first, with upstream tracking, a [gone] marker for branches whose upstream is no longer on the remote, the relative date, and the last commit subject. Offline; run git fetch -p first to refresh [gone].
List local branches whose upstream tracking ref has vanished since the last fetch/prune (merged, renamed, or deleted) — candidates to inspect, not proof of a merge. Offline and read-only.
Compact table of local branches ordered by tip commit date: relative date then name. Offline.
Probe GitHub SSH on port 22 and ssh.github.com on 443 with a bounded deadline, and report which route git currently uses. Read-only.

Route github.com SSH via ssh.github.com:443 for networks that stall port 22. Shows the exact change, asks [y/N], backs up ~/.ssh/config, installs a Groundwork-owned snippet plus one marked Include line, and fingerprint-checks GitHub's published host keys. --yes consents non-interactively.

Remove the managed port-443 fallback — Groundwork's override only; other SSH configuration of yours that selects 443 stays in force. Asks [y/N] first; backups are kept. --yes consents non-interactively.
Start a named tmux session.
Attach to an existing tmux session.
Start a project layout from a checked-in tmuxp config.
Capture the current tmux session as a starter layout config.
Start tmux without restoring the previous resurrect snapshot.
Update tmux plugins from a normal shell when TPM's tmux pane is hard to read.
Save a tmux-resurrect snapshot now.
Restore the last tmux-resurrect snapshot.
Update tmux plugins with TPM; press Esc or Enter if the update pane does not repaint.
Install or repair tmux plugins with TPM.
Reload tmux config.
Rename the active pane.
Rename the active window.
